item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Kabir writes the up-and-down sum $1+2+3+4+5+4+3+2+1$ with consecutive counting numbers that climb from $1$ to $5$ and then fall back to $1$. The figure shows those counts filling a $5$-by-$5$ square of unit tiles.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims explain why this sum equals $5^{2}$?

options.A: The climb from $1$ to $5$ and the fall back to $1$ fill the $5$-by-$5$ square of unit tiles in the figure, so the sum is $25$.
options.B: Any climb-and-fall list of whole numbers fills a $5$-by-$5$ square, even when the steps are not consecutive counting numbers.
options.C: Pairing the consecutive counts into the $5$-by-$5$ square in the figure shows why the sum equals $5^{2}$.
options.D: The consecutive climb-and-fall counts are produced by first writing the square value $25$.
